DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Nothing Under Us But Lake

STS-HS9-L4-1400P-HSSCIES-TTM-LAT-01 • HS Science Earth & Space Science 9th • Computational Representation of Earth Systems and Human Modifications
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Under the streets of Mexico City there is a lake that people drained. Five hundred years ago Tenochtitlan sat on Lake Texcoco, and floating gardens called chinampas fed the whole city. Engineers pulled the water out to stop the floods, and today parts of the city sink almost a foot every year. A computer model can run those years forward or backward and show what each choice did to the water, the land, and the people.
If you could move the slider back to 1519 and change one thing, what would you change, and what would the model show in 2026?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Ximena doing?
Look at the picture. Justify Ximena's action, infer its purpose, and argue what the year she reaches reveals about the whole mission.
2
What is Diego holding?
Look at the picture. Justify what Diego holds, infer its purpose, and argue what a sample of that water can and cannot prove.
3

Look at the picture. Justify the teacher's action, infer its purpose, and argue what a measurement between two years can reveal about the ground.
4
Where are these students? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Justify your answer about this place, infer its function, and argue which single detail is the strongest evidence.
5
Tell me about the big screen.
Look at the picture. Justify what the big screen shows, infer its argument, and compare its panels to explain what human choices changed.
6
What is Itzel wearing?
Look at the picture. Justify what Itzel is wearing, infer her role, and argue how the model she studies connects to the screens behind her.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
